questions.question: Name the four structures of an animal cell required in Grade 9 and give the function of each in one clause.
questions.expected_answer: Cell membrane: controls which substances enter and leave the cell because it is selectively permeable. Cytoplasm: jelly-like, mostly water, the site of the cell's chemical reactions and the medium holding the organelles. Nucleus: contains the DNA in chromosomes and so controls the activities of the cell. Mitochondria: release energy from glucose during cellular respiration, the powerhouses of the cell.

questions.question: A learner views a cheek cell with a 10× eyepiece and a 40× objective. Calculate the total magnification, and explain why methylene blue was added and why the learner should have started on the 4× objective.
questions.expected_answer: Total magnification = 10 × 40 = 400×. Methylene blue stains the nucleus dark blue and the cytoplasm pale blue so that the otherwise transparent structures become visible. The lowest objective gives a wide field of view to find and centre the cell before switching to 40×, where the field is tiny and the cell is easily lost.

questions.question: Explain why a muscle cell contains far more mitochondria than a skin cell, and state the word equation for the process taking place in mitochondria.
questions.expected_answer: Muscle cells contract and do far more work, so they need more energy released per second. Mitochondria are the site of cellular respiration, so more mitochondria release more energy. Word equation: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy. The energy is released from glucose, not made.
